snapshot_note: php::print_r / php::var_dump OVER ANY MADC TYPE (2026-08-17, merged to develop, UNRELEASED and INCOMPLETE — no version bump until the arc is done). Both are declared in <ns_php> as function TEMPLATES with NO definition anywhere: "any type" has no signature a host could satisfy, so the CIR builder GENERATES the dumper for whatever type the argument has (src/cir_dump.cpp) and the runtime carries only output primitives (src/rt/rt_dump.c — strict C11, printf not std::cout, ledger-registered so a -static-libmadc Mach-O program that dumps still links). A program that never dumps carries nothing: no runtime type-descriptor table exists. That shape also makes the owner's "cannot be exported" constraint STRUCTURAL (a declared-but-undefined template is an unresolved symbol for any C++ host) and is the FIRST deliberate exception to cpp-first-api.md, documented there. Recognition is a TAG, never a name: the parser stamps FuncDef::inline_builtin_kind (php_print_r / php_var_dump) at declaration registration — the same carrier std::addressof / std::forward / __destroy use, and one the forest already serializes (cir_arena builtin_kind_id), so a PACKED <ns_php> keeps it and nothing new had to be frozen. COVERED: scalars (signed/unsigned to 64 bits, floating, bool, char), C strings, structs and classes with access + inheritance, unions, anonymous unions, bit-fields, fixed arrays, char arrays as text, and POSITIONAL CONTAINERS (std::string as text, std::vector / std::array as arrays, a std::string member inside a struct) — the owner's own two examples. PHP IS THE ORACLE TO THE BYTE: php-cli 8.3.6 captured with cat -A, every print_r block identical for the corresponding PHP value (the 4-space entry indent, the 8-space step of a nested '(', the blank line after a nested block, [prot:protected] and [priv:Foo:private], 1 for true and NOTHING for false, and PHP's 14-significant-digit float including the '.0' mantissa PHP puts in an exponent form that C's %G drops). var_dump keeps PHP's frame and makes exactly ONE deliberate change — the real C/C++/madc type: double(3.5) not float(3.5), long(42), char *(2) "hi", struct Point(2), int[3](3). THE WALK NEVER COMPUTES OR EVEN READS A LAYOUT FACT: members are emitted as obj.member ACCESS nodes, so bit-field shift/mask, anonymous-aggregate transparency and base flattening keep their single owner and the dumper cannot drift from them; member_offsets is not consulted at all. Refusals are BY NAME of the type, never a guess (is_integer() is TRUE for a pointer, a pointer-to-data-member and a function pointer, and a SIMD vector's follows its element — any of those in the integer arm would print an address as a decimal). A PREREQUISITE CRASH fell out on the way in: for (int v : std::map<int,int>) SIGSEGV'd at (nil) where g++ AND clang both REJECT the source, because the iteration protocol matched size()/operator[] by NAME and then handed the loop counter to map::operator[](const key_type &) — a pointer parameter fed an integer. It is type-checked now (integral index by value or reference, integral size(), and no key_type alias), the element accessor delegates to class_subscript_addr_on (the ONE operator[] call builder, which reads the argument shape from the parameter and fixed a SECOND live crash on a container whose positional operator[] takes const long &), and new class_nullary_call is the one owner for an obj.size()-shaped call (emit_symbol-aware, which the hand-rolled Class__size was not).

known_pre_existing_gaps: SCRIPT `value` IS NOT YET THE 32-BYTE madc_value STRUCT (recorded 2026-08-17, owner: not to be taken on now). Symptom: `value f()` returned BY VALUE emits `int f()` and silently returns nothing (exit 0, empty output) — func_def's return-type arm -> type_list -> append_type_specs has no dtARRAY case and falls through to int. That is why php::print_r returns madc::value & rather than madc::value. CORRECTED PREMISE: a C type DOES exist — madc_value (include/madc_api.h:52) is a tagged 32-byte aligned(16) struct, and madc::value merely CONTAINS it plus two unique_ptr members (32+8+8 = 48 = the emitted long long[6]); the opaque-buffer lowering exists because of those OWNING C++ members, not a missing type. MEASURED: _array/_object are private with no friends and all 40 refs are in ONE file (src/madc_value.cpp) — 12 mutations, 28 reads; the cell finalizer is already wired and called from generated code (cir_builder.cpp:25789/25797); the is_array_object sites would mostly RETIRE. HARD PART: the class deep-copies the containers while the cell path shares, so the migration needs copy-on-write at those 12 sites — a semantic change with its own oracled tests. Full write-up: docs/plans/2026-06-12-type-table-value-abi-design.md section 9. Sibling defect, also open: assigning to a `value &` PARAMETER is wrongly rejected ('assignment of incompatible value').

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again). Proper fix: free the VLA at the backward goto. Separate future slice.
